extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting research manuscripts to Nature Portfolio journals (researchers across disciplines)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial policies and mandatory requirements for reporting and sharing data, materials, code, and experimental protocols for manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio journals. Covers data availability statements, mandatory repository deposition for specific data types, materials/code availability, pre-registration, and related reproducibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt availability of materials, data, code and protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to make materials, data, code, and associated protocols promptly available to readers without undue qualifications as a condition of publication in a Nature Portfolio journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any restrictions on availability must be disclosed to editors at submission and in the manuscript. Readers who encounter refusal should contact the chief editor; editors may refer matters to authors' institutions or publish formal corrections if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of restrictions at submission and in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Any restrictions on the availability of materials or information must be disclosed to the editors at the time of submission and also disclosed in the submitted manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors reserve the right to decline the study if restrictions are unduly prohibitive. Restrictions should be clearly stated (including if materials are to be distributed by a for‑profit company) and explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of completed reporting summary documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, manuscripts sent for review must include completed reporting summary documents (reporting summary will be made available to editors and reviewers and published with accepted manuscripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific reporting summaries are required for life sciences, behavioural & social sciences, ecology/evolution/environmental sciences, and some physical sciences areas (e.g., solar cells, claims of lasing). Adobe Reader required for advanced forms; flat reference copies available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory data availability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: All published manuscripts reporting original research in Nature Portfolio journals must include a data availability statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must make transparent the conditions of access to the 'minimum dataset' necessary to interpret, verify and extend the research. Supporting data must be made available to editors and reviewers on request at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum dataset accessibility and repository deposition preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum dataset necessary to interpret, verify and extend the research should be made available via deposition in public community/discipline-specific repositories, custom proprietary repositories, or general repositories like Figshare, Zenodo and Dryad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing large datasets as supplementary information is strongly discouraged; preferred approach is repository deposition. Scientific Data maintains a list of approved and recommended repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' responsibility for permissions and legal compliance for data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining all necessary permissions and ensuring compliance with local regulatory requirements for data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any restrictions on sharing must be discussed with the editor at submission who can decline manuscripts if conditions are unduly prohibitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement content: primary and referenced datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Data availability statements should include information about access to primary datasets (generated during the study) and referenced datasets (datasets analyzed in the study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where data are publicly available, accession codes or other unique identifiers should be provided. Provide details sufficient to locate and access datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial data sharing standards (ICMJE compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data availability statements for manuscripts reporting clinical trial data should follow ICMJE recommendations on clinical trial data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements must indicate whether individual de-identified participant data will be shared ('undecided' is not acceptable), what data will be shared, whether additional documents (protocol, SAP) will be available, when data will become available and for how long, and the access criteria (who, for what analyses, mechanism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability subject to controlled access
rubrics_metrics.description: If data are subject to controlled access (eg privacy, ethical/legal issues), the data availability statement should include reasons for controlled access and describe conditions of access precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact details for access requests, timeframe for response, restrictions on data use via data use agreements, and provide a copy or link to the data use agreement if requested. Editors may decline manuscripts with unduly prohibitive restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party data disclosure and peer-review access
rubrics_metrics.description: When data are obtained from third parties and cannot be made publicly available, restrictions should be clearly stated in the data availability statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must make data available for peer review, if requested, within terms of a data use agreement and in compliance with ethical and legal requirements. Identity of third party provider must be made known to editors at submission and peer review (exceptions possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary data availability obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors using proprietary data must ensure agreement with the third party data provider that datasets used in the study will be available under the conditions specified in the data availability statement (including whether the dataset will be available for a fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability for replication and verification purposes must be clearly stated in the data availability statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative data legal/regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies using administrative data (including data held by governments, local authorities and international organizations) must ensure that data use complies with local regulatory and legal frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe compliance measures and any access limitations resulting from legal frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of third-party data provider disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of the third party data provider must be made known to editors at time of submission and peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made where identity is not relevant or public release poses reputational or commercial risk; published examples are provided by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of data collection methods sufficient for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should provide information in the manuscript on their data collection methods sufficient to support peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data processing steps were performed by a third party outside authors' control, this should be clearly stated. Editors may decline manuscripts failing to provide sufficient information on data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation formatting and inclusion in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets deposited in repositories should be included as formal citations in the article reference list, including datasets generated during the study and existing datasets analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should include DataCite-recommended minimum information and follow Nature Portfolio style: author(s), title, publisher (repository name), and identifier. Dataset identifiers (DOIs) should be expressed as full URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory deposition for specific dataset types
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain types of data, submission to a community-endorsed public repository is mandatory; accession numbers must be provided in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of appropriate public repositories are listed by data type (see separate entries for specific data types and repositories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protein sequences deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Protein sequences must be deposited in an appropriate public repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repository example: UniProt. Accession numbers must be provided in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: DNA and RNA sequences deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DNA and RNA sequences must be deposited in public nucleotide sequence repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repositories: GenBank, DNA Data Bank of Japan (DDBJ), EMBL Nucleotide Sequence Database (ENA). Accession numbers must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: DNA and RNA sequencing data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DNA and RNA sequencing data must be deposited in sequencing data archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repositories: NCBI Trace Archive, NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA). Provide accession numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic polymorphisms deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Genetic polymorphism data should be deposited in appropriate variant databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repositories: dbSNP, dbVar, European Variation Archive (EVA). Include accession identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked genotype and phenotype data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked genotype and phenotype datasets should be submitted to repositories with appropriate access control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repositories: dbGaP, European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA). Use controlled access as needed and provide accession codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macromolecular structure deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Macromolecular structural data must be deposited in community structural biology repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repository: Worldwide Protein Data Bank (wwPDB). Provide accession numbers; official validation reports from wwPDB are required for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological magnetic resonance data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Magnetic resonance structural data should be deposited in an appropriate repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repository example: Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank (BMRB). Include accession numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electron microscopy data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Electron microscopy-derived density maps and coordinate data must be deposited in an electron microscopy repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repository: Electron Microscopy Data Bank (EMDB). Accessibility in repositories must be designated for immediate release on publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gene expression data deposition requirement (MIAME compliant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gene expression data must be MIAME compliant and deposited in community repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repositories: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), ArrayExpress. Provide accession codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallographic data for small molecules deposition and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts reporting new three-dimensional structures of small molecules from crystallographic analysis should include deposition of crystallographic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a .cif file, a structural figure with probability ellipsoids, submit structure factors, check using IUCr CheckCIF routine, include a PDF copy of CheckCIF output at submission and provide justification for any alerts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proteomics data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proteomics experimental data should be deposited in proteomics repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable repository: PRIDE. Provide accession numbers for submission and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred sharing of other datasets via public repositories (or general repositories)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to mandated datasets, the preferred way to share any datasets is via public repositories; where repositories do not exist, deposit in general-purpose repositories is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General repositories suggested: Figshare, Dryad, Zenodo. Scientific Data maintains a list of approved/recommended repositories by discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for DNA/protein sequences and short novel sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing reference genomes, the assembly must be made available in addition to sequence reads. Short stretches of novel sequence must include surrounding sequence context; sequences of small RNA probes central to conclusions must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deposition even for short novel sequences (epitopes, functional domains, markers, haplotypes) and provide contextual sequence information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked phenotype and genotype data for human subjects: controlled repository submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked phenotype and genotype data for human subjects should be submitted to a public repository with appropriate access control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain any restrictions on access for sensitive data and provide details of the conditions under which the data can be accessed or reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macromolecular structure validation and supporting data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Official validation reports from wwPDB are required for peer review. Atomic coordinates and related experimental data must be provided upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structure factors/restraints as appropriate; EM-derived density maps and coordinate data must be deposited with immediate release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallographic small-molecule submission technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Crystallographic manuscripts should include the .cif file, structure factors, IUCr CheckCIF output, and justification for any alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a structural figure with probability ellipsoids for Supplementary Information and a PDF copy of CheckCIF output at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials availability: unique materials must be made available
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to make unique materials promptly available to others without undue qualifications as a condition of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable payment to cover distribution costs is acceptable; any restrictions including distribution by for-profit companies must be clearly stated. Corresponding author is expected to be responsible for materials availability unless otherwise stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Resource Identification Initiative (RRIDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio supports the Resource Identification Initiative and encourages inclusion of unique identifiers (RRIDs) for key biological resources such as antibodies, cell lines, model organisms and tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to include RRIDs (e.g., Antibody: RRID:AB_2140114) and can find more information on the Resource Identification Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: New chemical compounds reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting new chemical compounds integral to conclusions must provide the chemical structure, synthesis and characterization with sufficient experimental details to allow reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include synthesis protocols, characterization data and other experimental details needed for others to reproduce synthesis and characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition of biological materials in established repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: For biological materials such as mutant strains and cell lines, authors are recommended to use established public repositories and provide accession numbers in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of repositories: Jackson Laboratory, EMMA, EUCOMM, KOMP, Addgene, RIKEN, Mutant Mouse Regional Resource Centers, ATCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell line reporting and authentication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must identify the source of cell lines (with catalog number if from a vendor/cell bank), report whether cell lines have been authenticated, include method used, results, and when authentication testing was last performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentication test results and mycoplasma testing status must be provided upon request. Deposition in repositories or establishment of a profile allowing authentication is strongly encouraged. Editors may demand data removal if justification for problematic lines is unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking for misidentified or cross-contaminated cell lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to check reagents against the list of known misidentified cell lines (ICLAC) and NCBI BioSample database; if using a listed cell line provide scientific justification and state the identity issue in Methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources and references on cell line authentication are provided; editors emphasize these requirements especially for cancer research and may enforce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of custom computer code and algorithms for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make available upon request to editors and reviewers any previously unreported custom computer code or algorithm used to generate results central to the paper's main claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will evaluate reasons to preclude code sharing and reserve the right to decline the paper if important code is unavailable. Journals offer optional services to support sharing via Code Ocean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code availability statement requirement and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: For all studies using custom code or mathematical algorithm deemed central to the conclusions, a 'Code availability' statement must be included indicating whether and how the code or algorithm can be accessed, including any restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code availability statements should be a separate section after the data availability statement but before the references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice for releasing code upon publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication, Nature Portfolio considers it best practice to release custom computer code in a way that allows readers to repeat published results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code should be deposited in DOI‑minting repositories such as Zenodo or Code Ocean and cited in the reference list. Authors are encouraged to manage subsequent versions and use an open-source-license approved by the Open Source Initiative. Full details about access and restrictions must be described in the Code Availability statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of code/algorithm/software when central to manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature journals undertake peer review of custom code, mathematical algorithms, and software when central to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For code/algorithm peer review, sharing of code/algorithm during peer review with editors and reviewers is required and inclusion of a Code Availability section on publication is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of step-by-step experimental protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to share step-by-step experimental protocols on a protocol sharing platform of their choice and to provide a DOI or other citation details in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature's protocols.io is suggested as a free, citable platform; links to help for publishing protocols are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for pre-registration and Registered Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support study pre-registration (including clinical trials) and pre-registration of analysis plans; details of pre-registration should be provided with submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered Reports (two-stage peer review where methods/analysis are pre-registered and peer reviewed before research is carried out) are available in specified journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming and evaluating replication studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio welcomes submission of replication studies that provide new insights into previously published results and evaluates these submissions with the same editorial standards as other submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replication studies should provide novel insight and meet the journal's editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials reporting: CONSORT, registration and reporting of registry number
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting phase II and phase III randomized controlled trials must refer to the CONSORT Statement; prospective clinical trials must be registered before patient enrollment in an appropriate public registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports not conforming to CONSORT may need revision before formal review. Suitable registries include ClinicalTrials.gov and registries listed by ICMJE/WHO. The trial registration number must be reported in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting prognostic studies and biospecimen standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting prognostic studies with tumor markers are encouraged to follow REMARK guidelines; for describing human biospecimens, refer to BRISQ and ensure at least Tier 1 characteristics are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BRISQ DOI provided; adhere to recommended reporting tiers for biospecimen information.
